src_text: Poutèt sa, granmoun ki pami nou yo kapab fè menm priyè sa a salmis la te fè nan moman li te kòmanse vin granmoun: Se ou menm ki espwa m, o Souvren Seyè Jewova [...] Pa voye m jete lè m vin granmoun.
reference: Therefore, the elderly among us can pray as the psalmist did when he began to grow old: “You are my hope, O Sovereign Lord Jehovah . . . Do not throw me away in the time of old age.”
explanation: It expresses the deep reliance older people place on God for continued care, dignity, and protection as they age.
expected_translation: So our elders can pray as the psalmist did when he grew old: “You are my hope, O Sovereign Lord Jehovah . . . Do not forsake me in my old age.” | Therefore, those of us who are elderly can pray as the psalmist did when he began to age: “You are my hope, O Sovereign Lord Jehovah . . . Do not abandon me when I am old.”

src_text: Seyè a voye yon moun pou sove pèp la . Se konsa , moun peyi Izrayèl yo soti anba men pèp Siri a . Yo tanmen viv ankò ak kè poze tankou anvan .
reference: The Lord sent a deliverer to the people , and the people of Israel escaped from under the hand of the Syrians , and they lived in peace again , as before .
explanation: It conveys the idea that divine intervention brings rescue from oppression and restores peace and normal life to a community.
expected_translation: The Lord sent a savior to rescue the people, and Israel lived in peace again | The Lord raised up a deliverer for the people, and the Israelites once more lived in peace

src_text: Men sa nou jwenn nan Eklezyas 12: 1: "Pandan ou jenn gason an, pa janm bliye Bondye ki te kreye ou la."
reference: Here is what we find in Ecclesiastes 12:1: "While you are young, never forget your Creator."
explanation: It encourages young people to remember and honor God early in life, before the distractions and responsibilities of adulthood take over.
expected_translation: While you’re young, never forget your Creator. | Remember your Creator while you are still young.

src_text: Poukisa li saj pou nou pa vanje lè y ap pèsekite nou?
reference: Why is it wise not to retaliate when we are persecuted?
explanation: It reflects the value of responding to persecution with restraint and wisdom rather than revenge, emphasizing patience, dignity, and moral strength.
expected_translation: Why is it wise not to get even when we’re persecuted? | Why is it wise to refrain from revenge when we’re persecuted?

src_text: Men sa Pyè te ekri: 'Toutotan mwen poko mouri, mwen kwè se yon devwa pou m fè nou chonje bagay sa yo pou dòmi pa pran nou.
reference: Peter wrote: 'I consider it right, while I am still alive, to remind you of these things so that you may not fall asleep.'
explanation: It means Peter feels a moral duty to keep reminding people of important truths while he is still alive, so they stay alert and don’t become spiritually or mentally complacent.
expected_translation: Peter wrote: “As long as I’m still alive, I feel it’s my duty to keep reminding you of these things so you don’t drift off.” | Peter wrote: “While I’m still here, I believe it’s my responsibility to keep bringing these things to mind so you stay alert.”

src_text: Poukisa fason Jonatan te reyaji anvè David la te diferan nèt ak fason Abnè te reyaji anvè David la?
reference: Why was Jonathan's reaction to David so different from Abner's?
explanation: It highlights a contrast in loyalty and attitude toward David, showing that Jonathan responded with friendship and support while Abner reacted in a more self-interested or opposing way.
expected_translation: Why did Jonathan respond to David so differently than Abner did? | Why was Jonathan’s reaction to David so different from Abner’s?

src_text: Kidonk, ann kontinye batay!
reference: So, let's keep fighting!
explanation: It conveys a spirited call to persevere together and keep pushing forward despite hardship.
expected_translation: So, let’s keep going! | Let’s keep up the fight!

src_text: Men non pitit Eyoud yo : Naaman , Ajija ak Gera . Yo te chèf branch fanmi ki t'ap viv nan zòn Geba a . Apre sa , yo mete yo deyò , y'al rete Manarat . Se Gera , papa Ouza ak Akiyoud , ki te mennen yo al rete Manarat la .
reference: The sons of Ehud : Naaman , Ahijah , and Gera . They were heads of families living in the area of Geba . They were then driven out and settled in Manahath . Gera , the father of Uzza and Ahihud , took them and settled there .
explanation: This expression reflects a biblical family genealogy and migration story, showing how clan leaders were displaced from one area and resettled under the guidance of a family patriarch.
expected_translation: The sons of Ehud were Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera, heads of families living in Geba. They were driven out and settled in Manahath. Gera, the father of Uzza and Ahihud, led them there | Ehud’s sons—Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera—were family heads in Geba. They were forced out and moved to Manahath, where Gera, father of Uzza and Ahihud, settled them

src_text: Apre sa, Jezi kite foul moun yo dèyè, li antre nan kay la. Disip li yo pwoche bò kote l, yo di l konsa: — Esplike nou parabòl move zèb nan jaden an.
reference: Then Jesus left the crowd and went into the house. His disciples came to him and said, “Explain to us the parable of the weeds in the field.”
explanation: It describes the disciples privately asking Jesus to clarify a teaching metaphor about harmful weeds growing among crops, reflecting a request for deeper spiritual understanding.
expected_translation: Then Jesus left the crowd and went into the house. His disciples came to him and said, “Explain the parable of the weeds in the field.” | After that, Jesus left the crowd and went inside the house. His disciples came to him and asked, “Explain to us the parable of the weeds in the field.”

src_text: W'ap pè moute sou bagay ki twò wo pou ou pa gen tèt vire . Menm mache nan granchemen ap yon danje pou ou . Tout cheve nan tèt ou ap vin blan , w'ap pèdi fòs kouray ou . Pa gen anyen ki ka fè l tounen ankò . W'ap desann nan dènye kay kote ou pral rete pou tou tan an . Lè sa a , moun ap mache rele nan tout lari .
reference: You will be afraid to climb on things that are too high for fear of dizziness. Even walking on the highway will be dangerous for you. All your hair will turn white, you will lose your strength. Nothing can bring it back. You will go down to the last house where you will stay forever. Then people will walk and shout in all the streets.
explanation: It is a poetic warning about old age and death, describing the gradual loss of strength and the final journey to the grave.
expected_translation: You’ll grow old and frail, and death will come for you. | You’ll become weak with age, until you’re laid to rest forever.

src_text: Mete sou sa, li te mete yon pano nan vitrin nan ki fè konnen nenpòt moun ki ka pwouve doktrin Trinite a biblik l ap peye moun sa a 100 liv ostralyen. Arthur te rejte doktrin sa a Bib la pa anseye a yon fason ki fèm.
reference: He also put up a sign in the window announcing that he would pay 100 Australian pounds to anyone who could prove the Bible-based doctrine of the Trinity. Arthur firmly rejected this unscriptural doctrine.
explanation: The expression highlights Arthur’s public, confident challenge to a widely debated religious doctrine, showing his firm opposition and willingness to reward anyone who could defend it from the Bible.
expected_translation: He also posted a sign in the window offering 100 Australian pounds to anyone who could prove the Trinity from the Bible. Arthur strongly rejected this unbiblical doctrine. | He put a notice in the shop window saying he would pay 100 Australian pounds to anyone who could prove the Trinity was taught in the Bible. Arthur firmly opposed this doctrine.

src_text: Moun lòt peyi yo ap achte figi m . Kou yo tande vwa m , yo obeyi m .
reference: Foreigners will buy my face. As soon as they hear my voice, they obey me.
explanation: It suggests that the speaker is so influential or authoritative that foreigners are eager to recognize, respect, or submit to them as soon as they hear them speak.
expected_translation: People from other countries will recognize me. As soon as they hear me speak, they listen to me. | Foreigners will respect my reputation. Once they hear my voice, they do what I say.

src_text: "KI SIY k ap siy prezans ou e k ap siy fen sistèm nan?" .
reference: WHAT will be the sign of your presence and the end of the system of things? .
explanation: It reflects a religious question about identifying the visible evidence that a divine presence has begun and that the current world order is coming to an end.
expected_translation: What will be the sign of your presence and the end of the world? | What will be the sign of your coming and the end of the age?

src_text: Jezi kite kote l te ye a . Antan li t'ap pase konsa , li wè yon nonm yo te rele Matye ki te chita nan biwo kontribisyon an . Jezi di l konsa : — Swiv mwen . Matye annik leve , li swiv Jezi .
reference: Jesus left that place and passed by and saw a man named Matthew sitting at the tax office. Jesus said to him, "Follow me." Matthew got up and followed Jesus.
explanation: This expression reflects the cultural and religious significance of a direct call to discipleship, showing Matthew’s immediate and wholehearted response to Jesus’ authority.
expected_translation: Jesus left there and, as he was walking along, saw a man named Matthew sitting at the tax collector’s booth. Jesus said to him, “Follow me.” Matthew got up at once and followed Jesus. | Jesus went on from there and saw a man called Matthew sitting at the tax office. Jesus told him, “Come, follow me,” and Matthew immediately got up and followed him.

src_text: IMAJINE w ap egzamine plan yon kay ou pral fè.
reference: IMAGINE that you are examining the plans for a house you are going to build.
explanation: It suggests carefully considering and visualizing a future project in advance, as if mentally reviewing the details before beginning.
expected_translation: Imagine you’re looking over the plans for a house you’re about to build | Picture yourself reviewing the blueprint for a house you plan to build

src_text: Se sa k te rive yon jèn sè ki rele Arielle, k ap viv ann Afrik delwès.
reference: That is what happened to a young sister named Arielle, who lives in West Africa.
explanation: It introduces a personal story about a young woman named Arielle living in West Africa, using a familiar narrative style to set up an account of something that happened to her.
expected_translation: That’s what happened to a young woman named Arielle, who lives in West Africa. | This is what happened to a young woman named Arielle, who lives in West Africa.

src_text: Ou mèt gen asirans Jewova pa atann pou nou pafè.
reference: Be assured that Jehovah does not expect us to be perfect.
explanation: It conveys a reassuring religious message that God is understanding and does not demand flawlessness from people, encouraging believers to accept their human limitations.
expected_translation: You can be sure Jehovah doesn’t expect us to be perfect | Rest assured, Jehovah doesn’t expect perfection from us

src_text: Yo te apwopriye paske li fasil pou yon moun remake yon lòt moun avid oswa yon lòt moun tonbe nan konvwatiz, men li pa fasil pou l rekonèt li menm li gen pwoblèm sa yo.
reference: They were appropriate because it is easy for a person to notice another person being greedy or falling into covetousness, but it is not easy to recognize that one has these problems themselves.
explanation: The expression highlights a common human tendency to spot faults like greed in others more easily than to admit or recognize the same flaws in oneself.
expected_translation: It’s easy to spot greed in others, but hard to see it in yourself. | People can easily notice greed in someone else, but not in themselves.

src_text: Sèn soti nan vizit Joselènnan Antaktik la.
reference: Scenes from Jocelin's visit to Antarctica.
explanation: This phrase refers to scenes from a visit to Antarctica, evoking an unusual, faraway, and likely adventurous or extraordinary experience.
expected_translation: Scenes from Jocelyn’s trip to Antarctica | Highlights from Jocelyn’s visit to Antarctica

src_text: Se konsa Moyiz sòti , li di pèp la tou sa Senyè a te di l . Li pran swasanndis nan chèf fanmi pèp Izrayèl la , li mete yo kanpe fè wonn kay Bondye a .
reference: So Moses went out and told the people all that the Lord had said to him , and he took seventy of the elders of Israel and set them around the house of God .
explanation: It describes Moses publicly delivering God’s instructions to the people and gathering the community’s senior leaders in a formal, sacred setting to witness and support the event.
expected_translation: So Moses went out and told the people everything the Lord had said to him | Moses then went out and relayed the Lord’s words to the people, and he gathered seventy of Israel’s elders around God’s house

src_text: Yo chase anpil demon, yo pase luil sou anpil moun malad e yo geri yo.
reference: They cast out many demons, anointed many sick people with oil, and healed them.
explanation: It describes a faith-healing ministry where religious leaders are seen as performing miracles by exorcising evil spirits, anointing the sick with oil, and bringing healing.
expected_translation: They drove out many demons, anointed many sick people with oil, and healed them | They cast out many demons, put oil on many sick people, and healed them

src_text: Li te wè lè Izrayelit yo te travèse rivyè Jouden an e li te wè mirak Jewova te fè lè sa a.
reference: He saw the Israelites cross the Jordan River and saw the miracles Jehovah performed at that time.
explanation: It means someone personally witnessed a remarkable historical event and can speak from direct experience about God’s powerful acts.
expected_translation: He witnessed the Israelites crossing the Jordan and the miracles Jehovah performed then | He saw the Israelites cross the Jordan and the miracles Jehovah worked at that time

src_text: Men , Seyè a , Bondye nou an , te refize koute Balaram , epi li fè madichon an tounen benediksyon pou nou , paske Seyè a , Bondye nou an , renmen nou .
reference: But the Lord our God refused to listen to Balaam and turned the curse into a blessing for us , because the Lord our God loves us .
explanation: It means that even when someone intends harm, God can overturn it and turn the situation into something good because of His love and care for His people.
expected_translation: But the Lord our God would not listen to Balaam and turned the curse into a blessing for us, because he loves us | The Lord our God refused Balaam’s curse and turned it into a blessing for us, because he loves us

src_text: Vòlè a vini sèlman pou l vòlè, pou l touye e pou l detwi. Mwen menm mwen vini pou moun yo ka gen lavi, e pou yo ka genyen l nètale.
reference: The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy. I have come that they may have life, and have it to the full.
explanation: This expression contrasts destructive intent with life-giving purpose, emphasizing that true goodness seeks to protect, restore, and bring people abundant life.
expected_translation: The thief comes only to steal, kill, and destroy. I came so they may have life, and have it abundantly. | The thief comes only to steal, kill, and destroy. I came so they may have life to the fullest.

src_text: Nan moman sa a, e pandan plizyè ane annapre, mwen te panse m te oblije rete djanm poutèt ti sè m nan. Se sa k fè mwen te antere sa m te santi.
reference: At that moment, and for many years afterward, I thought I had to stay strong for my little sister. That's why I buried my feelings.
explanation: The expression reflects the common cultural expectation of enduring hardship quietly and staying emotionally strong for family, especially to protect a younger sibling.
expected_translation: At the time, and for years after, I felt I had to be strong for my little sister, so I kept my feelings bottled up. | Back then and for a long time after, I believed I had to hold it together for my little sister, so I buried my emotions.

src_text: Y' al mande Seyè a si pa gen lòt moun ankò . Seyè a reponn : - Men Sayil kache dèyè pwovizyon yo !
reference: They asked the Lord if anyone was still there. The Lord answered, "Saul is hiding behind the provisions!"
explanation: It humorously suggests that someone who should be present or leading is instead hiding out of sight, avoiding attention or responsibility.
expected_translation: He’s hiding in plain sight | He’s hiding behind the supplies

src_text: Pwofèt Malaki te pale de enspeksyon sa a kòm yon netwayaj nan domèn espirityèl.
reference: The prophet Malachi spoke of this inspection as a spiritual cleansing.
explanation: It means the prophet Malachi is being used as a religious reference to describe a process of moral or spiritual purification.
expected_translation: The prophet Malachi described this as a spiritual purification | Malachi spoke of this as a cleansing of the spirit

src_text: Mesye sa yo menm , yo tankou bèt ki san konprann , k'ap viv dapre ensten yo epi ki la sou latè pou moun kenbe touye . Yo pale mal sou bagay yo pa konnen , yo gen pou yo peri menm jan ak bèt .
reference: These men are like brute beasts , living according to their instincts , and are on earth to be caught and killed . They speak evil of things they do not know , and they will perish like beasts .
explanation: The expression condemns people as reckless, ignorant, and morally base, comparing them to wild animals that act on instinct and are destined for destruction.
expected_translation: They’re like wild animals, driven by instinct and destined to be destroyed. | They talk trash about things they don’t understand, and they’ll end up perishing like animals.

src_text: Ocheya te ankouraje yo pou yo sipliye Jewova konsa: "Padone erè nou yo epi aksepte sa ki bon nan men nou. E nou menm bò kote pa nou n ap ofri pawòl ki sot nan bouch nou tankou jèn towo." — Och.
reference: Hosea urged them to plead with Jehovah: “Forgive our error and accept what is good from us. And we, for our part, will offer the young bulls of our mouths.”—Hos.
explanation: It means offering sincere prayers and praise to God as a heartfelt substitute for animal sacrifices, showing repentance and devotion.
expected_translation: Please forgive our sins and accept our praise. | Forgive our wrongdoing and receive our words of praise.

src_text: Lè w fè yon erè, menmsi se ta yon erè ki tou piti, se sèten ou t ap renmen pou lòt moun montre yo konprann ou oubyen menm bliye sa w fè a.
reference: When you make a mistake, even if it's a small one, you would surely like others to understand you or even forget what you did.
explanation: The expression reflects a cultural value of empathy and forgiveness, reminding people to treat others with the same understanding and leniency they would want for themselves when they make mistakes.
expected_translation: When you mess up, even a little, you’d want people to be understanding or just let it go. | If you make a mistake, even a small one, you’d hope others would show you some understanding and move on.

src_text: Pyè t'ap swiv Jezi yon ti jan lwen lwen , jouk yo rive nan lakou kay granprèt la . Li antre nan lakou a tou , li chita ak gad yo pou l' wè kouman sa t'apral fini .
reference: Peter followed Jesus at a distance , as far as the courtyard of the high priest . He also went in and sat with the guards to see the outcome .
explanation: It conveys Peter’s cautious, hesitant loyalty—staying close enough to follow Jesus, but far enough to avoid drawing attention to himself.
expected_translation: Peter followed Jesus from a distance, all the way to the high priest’s courtyard. He went inside and sat with the guards to see what would happen. | Peter trailed Jesus from far off to the high priest’s courtyard, then went in and sat with the guards to watch how it would all end.

src_text: Jan Seyè a te bay Moyiz lòd la , yo te tire osò devan Seyè a pou yo te ka konnen ki pòsyon ki tapral pou nèf branch fanmi ki te rete yo ak lòt mwatye branch nan fanmi Manase a .
reference: As the Lord commanded Moses , they cast lots before the Lord to determine the inheritance for the nine remaining tribes and the half - tribe of Manasseh .
explanation: It reflects a biblical practice of seeking God’s will by casting lots to fairly decide how land was allotted among the tribes.
expected_translation: They cast lots before the Lord to decide the inheritance for the nine remaining tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh | They drew lots before the Lord to determine the portions for the nine remaining tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh

src_text: Sepandan, apre chak frè te fin bay opinyon pa yo e yo te kite lespri sen gide yo pou yo pran yon desizyon, yo pa t plede ensiste sou ide yo te gen nan tèt yo a.
reference: However, after each brother had expressed his opinion and allowed holy spirit to guide them in making a decision, they did not insist on their own ideas.
explanation: It reflects a culture of respectful group decision-making, where individuals share their views but ultimately yield to collective guidance rather than stubbornly pushing their own opinions.
expected_translation: However, after everyone shared their views and let holy spirit guide the decision, they didn’t insist on their own ideas. | After each brother gave his opinion and let holy spirit lead the way, they didn’t push their own ideas.

src_text: Ki vrè rezon ki fè ti jèm nan seche nan dezyèm kalite tè ki nan egzanp Jezi a?
reference: What is the real reason why the little seed withers in the second type of soil in Jesus' parable?
explanation: It asks for the deeper spiritual reason a small seed fails to thrive in Jesus’ parable, using the image of different kinds of soil to talk about how people receive faith.
expected_translation: What’s the real reason the seed withers in the second kind of soil in Jesus’ parable? | Why does the seed dry up in the second type of soil in Jesus’ parable?

src_text: Apre sa, li di: "Jezi, sonje m lè w vin wa."
reference: Then he said, "Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom."
explanation: A humble plea for mercy and inclusion, expressing faith that Jesus has authority to save and remember the speaker in his future kingdom.
expected_translation: Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom. | Lord, remember me when you come into your kingdom.

src_text: Lè m te sot nan kongrè a, mwen te detèmine pou m defann lafwa m nan lekòl mwen.
reference: When I left the convention, I was determined to defend my faith at my school.
explanation: It conveys a strong personal commitment to stand up for one’s religious beliefs in a school setting, reflecting the importance of faith and conviction in daily life.
expected_translation: When I came back from the convention, I was determined to stand up for my faith at school. | After the convention, I was determined to defend my faith at school.

src_text: Berya te papa Refak ki te papa Rechèf . Rechèf te papa Tela ki te papa Takan .
reference: Beriah was the father of Rephah, who was the father of Resheph, who was the father of Telah, who was the father of Tahan.
explanation: It conveys a genealogical lineage, emphasizing family ancestry and the passing of identity through successive generations.
expected_translation: Beriah was the father of Rephah, who was the father of Resheph, who was the father of Telah, who was the father of Tahan. | Beriah fathered Rephah, Rephah fathered Resheph, Resheph fathered Telah, and Telah fathered Tahan.

src_text: Nan yon zòn ann Afrik, yo te gaye yon bann vye manti sou Temwen Jewova yo. Pa egzanp, yo te di se Dyab la y ap sèvi.
reference: In one area of Africa, many false accusations were spread about Jehovah’s Witnesses, such as that they served the Devil.
explanation: It describes how Jehovah’s Witnesses were the target of harmful rumors and false accusations in an African community, reflecting local suspicion and religious misunderstanding.
expected_translation: In one part of Africa, a lot of false rumors were spread about Jehovah’s Witnesses, including claims that they served the Devil | In an area of Africa, many lies were circulated about Jehovah’s Witnesses, such as saying they were serving the Devil

src_text: Paske, tout moun lespri Bondye ap gide se pitit Bondye yo ye.
reference: For all who are led by the Spirit of God are children of God.
explanation: It conveys the Christian belief that those guided by God’s Spirit are recognized as part of God’s family and live under His care and authority.
expected_translation: All who are led by God’s Spirit are God’s children | Those guided by the Spirit of God are children of God

src_text: Sepandan, istoryen yo dakò pa gen okenn moun ki konnen dat Jezi te fèt.
reference: However, historians agree that no one knows the exact date of Jesus' birth.
explanation: It means that, according to historical understanding, Jesus’ exact birthday is unknown and cannot be determined with certainty.
expected_translation: However, historians agree that no one knows the exact date Jesus was born | Still, historians agree that nobody knows Jesus’ exact birthday

src_text: Apre sa , Jezi pran senk pen yo ak de pwason yo . Li leve je li anlè , li rann Bondye gras . Epi li separe pen yo bay disip yoditribye bay moun yo . Li fè menm bagay la tou ak de pwason yo .
reference: Then Jesus took the five loaves and the two fish , looked up and gave thanks , and distributed the loaves to the disciples and the crowds . He did the same with the two fish .
explanation: This expression reflects a biblical scene of Jesus giving thanks before sharing food, symbolizing gratitude, generosity, and the miraculous provision of enough for everyone.
expected_translation: Then Jesus took the five loaves and two fish, looked up to heaven, gave thanks, and handed them out to the disciples and the crowd. | Jesus took the five loaves and two fish, gave thanks, and distributed them to the disciples and the people.

src_text: Mwen kontan anpil dèske m ede anpil moun pou yo vwe lavi yo bay Jewova e pou yo batize.
reference: I have had the great joy of helping many people to dedicate their lives to Jehovah and get baptized.
explanation: The expression reflects the deep joy and religious fulfillment felt in helping others commit their lives to Jehovah and publicly join the faith through baptism.
expected_translation: I’ve been very happy to help many people dedicate their lives to Jehovah and get baptized | It has brought me great joy to help many people dedicate their lives to Jehovah and be baptized

src_text: Li te yon bèl distans lè li wè Jezi . Li kouri , li vin mete ajenou devan li .
reference: He saw Jesus from a great distance away, and ran and knelt before him.
explanation: The expression conveys deep respect and reverence, showing that the person urgently approaches Jesus and kneels as an act of humility and honor.
expected_translation: He saw Jesus from far away and ran up to kneel before him | From a distance, he saw Jesus, ran over, and knelt down before him

src_text: Se kòmsi lavi m te fini.
reference: It was as if my life was over.
explanation: It conveys a deep sense of despair or hopelessness, as if everything in one’s life has collapsed or lost meaning.
expected_translation: It felt like my life was over | I felt like my life was over

src_text: Yo te meprize l, e yo te konsidere l tankou li pa t vo anyen.
reference: They despised him, and considered him worthless.
explanation: It conveys deep contempt and social rejection, treating someone as if they had no value or dignity.
expected_translation: They looked down on him and treated him like he was worthless | They despised him and saw him as having no value

src_text: David te wè sa Bondye ta pral fè a. Se konsa li te di Kris la te gen pou l leve sòti vivan nan lanmò lè l di : Yo p'ap kite l kote mò yo ye a. Kò li p'ap tounen pouriti .
reference: David saw what God was going to do. So he spoke about the resurrection of the Christ, saying, "He was not abandoned to Hades, nor did his flesh see corruption."
explanation: It means David was understood to be prophetically foretelling Jesus’ resurrection, emphasizing that God would not leave him in the realm of the dead or let his body decay.
expected_translation: David saw what God was going to do. So he spoke about Christ’s resurrection, saying, “He was not left in the grave, and his body did not decay.” | David foresaw what God would do, and he spoke of Christ’s resurrection: “He was not abandoned to the realm of the dead, nor did his body rot.”

src_text: Bon konprann ou ak richès ou pi plis pase sa yo te di m lan. .
reference: Your wisdom and wealth exceed what I was told.
explanation: It is a respectful compliment meaning the person is even more impressive in intelligence and prosperity than their reputation suggested.
expected_translation: You’re even wiser and wealthier than I’d heard | Your wisdom and riches are greater than I was told

src_text: Li te di tou: "Moun ki gen imilite yo ap posede tè a, e y ap kontan anpil akoz yo pral viv nan yon lapè total."
reference: He also said: “The meek will possess the earth, and they will indeed find their exquisite delight in the abundance of peace.”
explanation: It conveys the idea that humble, gentle people are ultimately blessed with lasting security, joy, and deep peace.
expected_translation: The humble will inherit the earth and enjoy great peace | The meek will possess the land and live in perfect peace

src_text: Sa vle di, Bondye sèvi ak Jezi pou l reyalize objektif li.
reference: This means that God uses Jesus to accomplish his purpose.
explanation: It reflects a Christian belief that Jesus is God’s chosen means for carrying out divine plans and fulfilling God’s will.
expected_translation: This means God uses Jesus to fulfill his purpose | God uses Jesus to carry out his plan

src_text: Li te mande disip yo pou priye konsa: Se pou wayòm ou an vini.
reference: He asked his disciples to pray like this: Your kingdom come.
explanation: It reflects a Christian prayer asking for God’s reign and justice to be established in people’s lives and in the world.
expected_translation: Your kingdom come | May your kingdom come

src_text: Tande, san frè w la ap rele nan pye m etan l atè a. .
reference: Listen, your brother's blood is crying out at my feet as he lies on the ground.

src_text: Vrèmanvre, si nou fidèl ak Jewova e nou suiv enstriksyon li ban nou yo pa mwayen òganizasyon l lan, l ap ban nou lavi ki pap janm fini an e l ap fidèl avè n nètale!

expected_translation: You may ask yourself: “Am I trying not to be part of the world?” | “Do I make an effort to stay separate from the world?”

reference: The Bible tells God’s people: “Repudiate ungodliness, . . . reject worldly desires, and . . . live with soundness of mind, righteousness, and godly devotion amid this present system of things, while we await the happy hope and glorious revelation of the great God and our Savior, Christ Jesus. src_text: Ki sa Jezi ap fè jodi a, e ki kesyon sa soulve?

explanation: It reflects a reflective Christian way of asking what Jesus is presently doing in believers’ lives and in the world, while inviting deeper questions about faith, purpose, and divine action today.
expected_translation: What is Jesus doing today, and what questions does that raise? | What is Jesus doing today, and what questions does that bring up?

src_text: Èske sa deja rive, ou achte yon kado pou yon bon zanmi epi, lè l resevwa l, ou wè kontantman ak apresyasyon parèt sou vizaj li?

expected_translation: Have you ever bought a gift for a close friend and seen how happy and grateful they were when they got it? | Have you ever given a good friend a gift and watched their face light up with joy and appreciation?

explanation: This expression reflects a Christian communal ideal of keeping Christ’s teachings central in daily life, encouraging mutual guidance, worship, and gratitude within the faith community.
expected_translation: Let Christ’s message live richly in your hearts, teaching and encouraging one another with wisdom, singing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs with thankful hearts to God | Let the word of Christ dwell richly among you, as you teach and counsel one another wisely, singing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs with gratitude to God

src_text: Gen lòt tou ki renmen ak moun ki pa Temwen Jewova.
reference: There are also others who are in love with people who are not Jehovah's Witnesses.
explanation: It refers to people who are romantically involved with someone outside the Jehovah’s Witness faith, highlighting a relationship that crosses religious boundaries.
expected_translation: There are others who are dating non-Witnesses. | Some are in relationships with people who aren’t Jehovah’s Witnesses.

src_text: Mechan yo pase tout lavi yo nan tèt chaje . Moun k'ap plede maltrete parèy yo p'ap viv lontan .
reference: The wicked spend their whole lives in trouble , and those who oppress their neighbors will not live long .
explanation: It conveys the moral belief that people who mistreat others bring hardship on themselves and will ultimately face a short, troubled life.
expected_translation: Wicked people live in constant trouble, and those who mistreat others won’t live long | Evil-doers spend their lives in misery, and oppressors don’t last long

src_text: Yon lòt danje nou dwe evite se danje yo pale de li nan Eklezyas 7: 16 la (NW): Pinga w vin jis aleksè, ni pa montre w saj depase.
reference: Another danger we must avoid is the one mentioned at Ecclesiastes 7:16: “Do not become righteous overmuch, nor show yourself excessively wise.”
explanation: It warns against becoming self-righteous or overly proud of one’s own wisdom, urging balance and humility instead of extremes.
expected_translation: Another danger we must avoid is the one mentioned at Ecclesiastes 7:16: “Do not be overly righteous or overly wise.” | Another danger we must avoid is the one mentioned at Ecclesiastes 7:16: “Don’t be self-righteous or act like you know it all.”

src_text: Sèvi ak apendis ki nan Labib — Tradiksyon monn nouvo a si l disponib nan yon lang ou konnen.
reference: Use the appendix in the New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures if it is available in a language you know.
explanation: It advises readers to consult the appendix of the New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures, if they can read that language, as a helpful study resource.
expected_translation: Use the appendix in the New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures if you have it in a language you know | If available in a language you know, use the appendix in the New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures

src_text: Gen yon istoryen juif ki rele Jozèf ki fè konnen, pandan kanpay militè Aleksann t ap fè nan zòn Jerizalèm, yo te montre l pwofesi sa a e li te kwè pwofesi sa a gen rapò avè l.
reference: Jewish historian Josephus states that during Alexander's military campaign in the Jerusalem area, he was shown this prophecy and believed that it applied to him.
explanation: This refers to a historical-religious tradition in which Josephus says Alexander the Great was shown a Jewish prophecy and interpreted it as predicting his own rise, highlighting the belief that ancient prophecies could be seen as relevant to current rulers and events.
expected_translation: Jewish historian Josephus says that during Alexander’s campaign near Jerusalem, he was shown this prophecy and believed it referred to him. | Josephus, the Jewish historian, says that while Alexander was campaigning around Jerusalem, he was shown this prophecy and thought it applied to him.

src_text: Men sa Pòl te di ansyen nan kongregasyon Efèz yo: Fè atansyon ak tèt nou e ak tout twoupo lespri sen etabli nou siveyan sou li a, pou nou pran swen kongregasyon Bondye a, kongregasyon li achte ak san pwòp Pitit li a.
reference: Paul told the elders of the Ephesian congregation: “Pay attention to yourselves and to all the flock, among which the holy spirit has appointed you overseers, to shepherd the congregation of God, which he purchased with the blood of his own Son.”
explanation: This expression emphasizes the serious spiritual responsibility of congregation elders to care for both themselves and the community, highlighting that their role is seen as a sacred appointment to protect and guide people whom God values deeply.
expected_translation: Paul told the elders of the Ephesian congregation: “Keep watch over yourselves and over the whole flock, in which the holy spirit has made you overseers, to care for God’s congregation, which he bought with the blood of his own Son.” | Paul said to the elders of the Ephesian congregation: “Be on guard for yourselves and for all the flock, over which the holy spirit appointed you as overseers, to shepherd God’s congregation, which he purchased with the blood of his own Son.”

src_text: Sepandan, olye pou n ap fache pou nenpòt ti krik ti krak, sa ki kapab fè n kraze lapè ki gen nan kongregasyon an, ann eseye imite Jewova epi annou padone youn lòt ak tout kè nou toutpandan n ap kontinye travay kòtakòt nan sèvis Jewova a.
reference: However, rather than becoming angry over minor disagreements, which could disrupt the peace of the congregation, let us strive to imitate Jehovah and forgive one another from the heart as we continue to work side by side in Jehovah’s service.
explanation: The expression encourages people to avoid letting small disputes damage community harmony and instead to follow Jehovah’s example by forgiving each other sincerely and continuing to cooperate peacefully.
expected_translation: Instead of getting upset over little things that could disturb the congregation’s peace, let’s imitate Jehovah and forgive one another wholeheartedly as we keep working together in his service. | Rather than letting minor disagreements make us angry and upset the congregation’s peace, let’s follow Jehovah’s example, forgive each other sincerely, and keep serving side by side.

src_text: Konesans sa a ede anpil moun vin pwòp nan domèn moral, li fè yo kite move abitid yo te genyen, li fè yo vin gen pi bon relasyon ak fanmi yo e yo vin gen pi bon relasyon ak Bondye, li menm ki Mèt Bib la.
reference: This knowledge has helped many to become morally clean, to break free from bad habits, to improve their relationships with their families, and to have a better relationship with God, the Author of the Bible.
explanation: The expression highlights the idea that gaining spiritual knowledge can lead people to moral improvement, healthier family life, and a closer relationship with God.
expected_translation: This knowledge has helped many become morally clean, break bad habits, improve family relationships, and draw closer to God, the Bible’s Author | This knowledge has helped many live morally clean lives, leave bad habits behind, strengthen family ties, and build a better relationship with God, the Bible’s Author

src_text: Lefètke Jewova pa t deside montre menm kote a se li menm ki Souvren an, li te bay Satan tan pou l pwouve sa l te di yo.
reference: By not immediately asserting his sovereignty, Jehovah gave Satan time to prove his claim.
explanation: It means that Jehovah allowed Satan a period of time to demonstrate whether his challenge was true, rather than immediately proving his own authority.
expected_translation: By not immediately asserting his sovereignty, Jehovah gave Satan time to prove his claim. | Jehovah didn’t right away prove his sovereignty, so Satan was given time to back up what he said.

src_text: Dapre sèman li te fè bay Abraram , zansèt nou an .
reference: According to the oath he swore to our father Abraham .
explanation: This expression refers to God’s solemn promise to Abraham, emphasizing faithfulness to a sacred covenant passed down as part of the community’s spiritual heritage.
expected_translation: As he promised our ancestor Abraham | In keeping with the oath he made to our father Abraham

src_text: Ki jan Pyè te 'bay frè l yo fòs'?
reference: How did Peter “strengthen his brothers”?
explanation: It means Peter encouraged and spiritually supported his fellow believers, helping them stay strong in their faith.
expected_translation: How did Peter encourage his brothers? | How did Peter support his brothers?

src_text: Epi li di : - Poukisa w'ap koute moun k'ap di ou m'ap chache fè malè sou ou ?
reference: And he said: - Why do you listen to those who tell you that I am trying to harm you?
explanation: It expresses a warning against believing gossip or rumors that may wrongly make someone distrust a person’s intentions.
expected_translation: Why are you listening to people saying I’m trying to hurt you? | Why do you believe people who say I mean you harm?

src_text: Men, e lè gen konfli ant sa Bondye mande ak sa gouvènman yo mande?
reference: But what if there is a conflict between what God requires and what governments require?
explanation: It reflects a common moral dilemma about whether religious obligations should take precedence over government laws when the two seem to conflict.
expected_translation: But what if God’s commands conflict with government demands? | What if what God asks for clashes with what the government requires?

src_text: Pandan m te nan yon kan yo te fè pou moun ki imigre nan peyi a, mwen te resevwa yon liv Temwen Jewova yo te fè pou moun etidye Bib la.
reference: While I was in a camp for immigrants, I received a Bible study book produced by Jehovah's Witnesses.
explanation: It refers to someone receiving a Bible study publication from Jehovah’s Witnesses while staying in an immigrant camp, highlighting outreach to migrants through religious literature.
expected_translation: While I was in an immigrant camp, I got a Bible study book from Jehovah’s Witnesses. | While staying in a camp for immigrants, I received a Bible study book published by Jehovah’s Witnesses.

src_text: Se sa k fè Izkiya te antre nan tanp Jewova a e li te kòmanse priye. Men sa l te di: "Senyè, Bondye nou an, tanpri, delivre nou anba men Senakerib, pou tout nasyon ki sou latè ka konnen se ou menm sèl, Senyè, ki Bondye." — 2 Wa 19: 14 - 19.
reference: So Hezekiah entered the temple of Jehovah and began to pray. He said: “O Jehovah our God, please save us from the hand of Sennacherib, so that all the peoples of the earth may know that you, Jehovah, are God alone.” —2 Kings 19:14-19.
explanation: This expression reflects a deeply religious appeal for divine rescue in a crisis, emphasizing both trust in God’s protection and the desire for God’s name and power to be publicly recognized among all nations.
expected_translation: So Hezekiah went into Jehovah’s temple and began to pray. He said: “O Jehovah our God, please rescue us from Sennacherib’s hand, so that all the nations on earth may know that you alone are God.” —2 Kings 19:14-19. | Hezekiah entered Jehovah’s temple and prayed, saying: “Jehovah our God, please deliver us from Sennacherib, so all the peoples of the earth will know that you alone are God.” —2 Kings 19:14-19.

src_text: Men sa l ajoute: "Men, avèk jantiyès, mari m te ede m konprann nou pa responsab pitit nou an ankò e n pa dwe antre nan zafè l."
reference: She adds: "But, with kindness, my husband helped me understand that we are no longer responsible for our child and should not interfere in his affairs."
explanation: The expression reflects a respectful family boundary in which parents recognize their adult child’s independence and avoid meddling in his personal decisions.
expected_translation: She says, “But my husband gently helped me realize that our child is grown and we shouldn’t вмешаться in his life.” | She adds, “But kindly, my husband made me understand that our child is no longer our responsibility and we should stay out of his business.”

src_text: Nan Paradi Jewova pral tabli sou tè a nan yon tikras tan ankò, pap manke okazyon pou nou pwofite jenewozite Jewova totalman, ansanm ak konpayi agreyab tout moun ki respekte egzijans li yo ki jis. — Sòm 145: 16; Izayi 25: 6; 2 Korentyen 7: 1.
reference: In the Paradise that Jehovah will soon establish on earth, there will be no shortage of opportunities to benefit fully from Jehovah’s generosity, including the pleasant company of all who meet his righteous requirements. —Psalm 145:16; Isaiah 25:6; 2 Corinthians 7:1.
explanation: The expression reflects a Jehovah’s Witness belief in a future earthly Paradise where God’s generosity will be fully enjoyed in a peaceful community of righteous people.
expected_translation: In the Paradise Jehovah will soon establish on earth, we’ll have many opportunities to enjoy his generosity to the full, along with the pleasant company of all who live by his righteous standards. | In the earthly Paradise Jehovah will soon bring about, there will be no lack of chances to fully benefit from his generosity and enjoy the pleasant company of everyone who meets his righteous requirements.

src_text: Se konsa Pilat pran desizyon pou l' ba yo sa yo te mande a .
reference: So Pilate decided to give them what they asked for.
explanation: It conveys that Pilate ultimately yielded to the crowd’s request and made a decision in their favor.
expected_translation: So Pilate decided to grant their request. | So Pilate chose to give them what they wanted.

src_text: Menm jan an tou, NOU menm jèn gason, se pou NOU soumèt devan ansyen yo. Men, se NOU tout ki pou abiye NOU ak imilite nan relasyon NOU youn ak lòt, paske Bondye kont moun ki ògeye yo, men li bay moun ki enb yo favè san parèy la.
reference: Likewise, you younger men, be in subjection to the older men. All of you, clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, because God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.
explanation: This expression teaches that younger people should show respect and deference to elders, while everyone should practice humility and mutual consideration in the community.
expected_translation: Likewise, you younger men, submit yourselves to your elders. All of you, clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, because God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble. | In the same way, you younger men should yield to your elders. And all of you should put on humility in your dealings with one another, for God resists the proud but gives grace to the humble.

src_text: 17, 18. a Ki sa lèt Jezi te ekri sèt kongregasyon ann Azi Minè yo revele sou konpreyansyon pwofon li genyen?
reference: 17, 18. a What do Jesus’ letters to the seven congregations in Asia Minor reveal about his depth of understanding?
explanation: It asks what Jesus’ messages to the seven congregations show about how deeply he understands their real spiritual condition and needs.
expected_translation: What do Jesus’ letters to the seven congregations in Asia Minor show about how deeply he understands things? | What do Jesus’ letters to the seven congregations in Asia Minor reveal about the depth of his understanding?

src_text: Okontrè, li te bay Jòb posiblite pou l pwouve entegrite l, pou l montre adorasyon l t ap ba l la te soti nan yon kè ki pwòp e ki pa egoyis.
reference: Rather, he gave Job the opportunity to prove his integrity, to show that his worship came from a pure, unselfish heart.
explanation: It means that Job was allowed to demonstrate his sincerity and moral integrity, showing that his devotion was genuine and selfless rather than motivated by personal gain.
expected_translation: Instead, he gave Job the chance to prove his integrity, to show that his worship came from a pure, selfless heart. | Rather, he allowed Job to demonstrate his integrity and prove that his worship came from a pure, unselfish heart.

src_text: Se Senyè a menm ki te bay Moyiz regleman sa yo , sou mòn Sinayi nan mitan dezè a , jou li te mande moun pèp Izrayèl yo pou yo fè ofrann ba li .
reference: The Lord himself gave these regulations to Moses on Mount Sinai in the wilderness , on the day he commanded the Israelites to present their offerings to him .
explanation: It emphasizes that these laws are divinely given and therefore carry sacred authority for the Israelites, rooted in their covenant relationship with God.
expected_translation: The Lord gave these instructions to Moses on Mount Sinai in the wilderness, when he told the Israelites to bring their offerings to him | The Lord himself gave Moses these laws on Mount Sinai in the desert, the day he commanded the Israelites to present their offerings

src_text: Men sa li di: "Menm jan mwen vivan, [...] mwen pran plezi, non pa nan lanmò mechan an, men pou moun ki mechan an vire kite chemen l e vrèman pou li rete vivan." .
reference: He says: “As long as I live, […] I take delight, not in the death of the wicked, but in that the wicked turn from his way and keep living.” .
explanation: It expresses the idea that God values repentance and a person’s return to the right path more than punishment, showing mercy and a desire for life over death.
expected_translation: I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but rather that they turn from their ways and live | I delight in seeing the wicked turn from their evil ways and live

src_text: Se pou rezon sa a, Jezi Kris te di yo avèk franchiz: Gade!
reference: That is why Jesus Christ said to them boldly: Look!
explanation: It conveys a direct, emphatic way of speaking that signals Jesus is about to make an important point and wants the listeners’ full attention.
expected_translation: That’s why Jesus Christ told them plainly: Look! | That’s why Jesus Christ said to them openly: Look!

src_text: Apre yon gwo kanpay predikasyon espesyal, li te di disip li yo: "Nou menm, vin yon kote apa pou nou pran yon ti repo." — Mak 6: 31, 32.
reference: After a special preaching campaign, he told his disciples: “Come, you yourselves, privately into a secluded place and rest up a little.” —Mark 6:31, 32.
explanation: It conveys the idea of stepping away from public activity to a quiet, private place for rest and recovery after intense work.
expected_translation: After a special preaching campaign, he told his disciples: “Come away with me to a quiet place and get some rest.” | After a special preaching campaign, he told his disciples: “Let’s go off somewhere private and take a little rest.”

src_text: Se sa k fè Jan Batis te rele l "ti mouton Bondye a k'ap wete peche moun sou tout latè".
reference: That is why John the Baptist called him "the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the whole world".
explanation: It means John the Baptist identified Jesus as a sacred, sacrificial figure sent by God to remove humanity’s sins.
expected_translation: That’s why John the Baptist called him “the Lamb of God who takes away the sins of the world” | That’s why John the Baptist referred to him as “the Lamb of God who takes away the sins of the world”

src_text: Nou ka fè sa nan reyinyon yo lè n priye Jewova, lè n chante pou li ak lè n pale de li.
reference: We can do this at meetings by praying to Jehovah, singing to him, and talking about him.
explanation: It reflects the importance of worship meetings in Jehovah’s Witness culture, where prayer, singing, and speaking about God are seen as shared acts of devotion and community faith.
expected_translation: We can do this at meetings by praying to Jehovah, singing to him, and talking about him. | At meetings, we can do this by praying to Jehovah, singing to him, and speaking about him.

src_text: Y'a mòde an trèt, y'a fè kòlè fasil, lògèy va gonfle lestonmak yo.
reference: They will bite treacherously, they will be easily angered, and their breasts will be puffed up with pride.
explanation: It describes people as being deceitful, quick-tempered, and arrogant, warning that such attitudes make them dangerous and hard to trust.
expected_translation: They’ll be treacherous, quick-tempered, and full of pride | They’ll be deceitful, easily angered, and arrogant

src_text: Mwen menm Pyè , apot Jezikri , mwen ekri llèt sa a pou nou tout ki fè pati pèp Bondye te chwazi a epi ki egzile nan peyi Pon , Galasi , Kapadòs , Lazi ak Bitini .
reference: Peter , an apostle of Jesus Christ , to all of you who are chosen by God and are exiles in Pontus , Galatia , Cappadocia , Asia , and Bithynia .
explanation: This is a formal biblical greeting that identifies the writer as an apostle and addresses believers as God’s chosen people living as outsiders or dispersed communities across several regions.
expected_translation: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, writes to God’s chosen people living as exiles in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia | Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to God’s elect who are scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia

src_text: Sepandan, si w bay frè ou konfye responsablite a yon ti libète, petèt l ap vin gen konfyans nan tèt li e l ap vin gen eksperyans.
reference: However, if you give the brother you entrust with responsibility a little freedom, he may gain confidence and experience.
explanation: The expression reflects a cultural value of trusting someone with responsibility while allowing some independence, since giving them room to act is seen as a way to build confidence and practical experience.
expected_translation: If you give him a little freedom, he may build confidence and gain experience. | Give him some room, and he may become more confident and experienced.

src_text: Nou tout ap goumen ak pwòp enpèfeksyon pa nou ansanm ak enpèfeksyon lòt moun.
reference: We all struggle with our own imperfections as well as the imperfections of others.
explanation: It reflects a communal, empathetic view of life that acknowledges everyone’s flaws and encourages patience and mutual understanding in dealing with one another.
expected_translation: We all have our flaws and have to deal with other people’s flaws too | Everyone has imperfections, including ourselves and those around us

src_text: Nan kòmansman ane 1933, wa Sobhuza te konn pran plezi tande pyonye yo lè yo te konn vizite l nan vilaj li te abite a.
reference: In early 1933, King Sobhuza enjoyed listening to the pioneers when they visited him in his village.
explanation: The sentence reflects a respectful historical account of a king receiving visitors in his village and valuing their stories or presence, highlighting the importance of hospitality and oral exchange in the local culture.
expected_translation: In early 1933, King Sobhuza liked hearing the pioneers when they came to visit him in his village. | In the beginning of 1933, King Sobhuza enjoyed listening to the pioneers during their visits to his village.

src_text: Geoffrey Jackson, youn nan manm Kolèj santral la, t ap prezide reyinyon sa a.
reference: Geoffrey Jackson, a member of the Governing Body, presided over this meeting.
explanation: It means Geoffrey Jackson was the person officially leading and conducting the meeting in a position of authority.
expected_translation: Geoffrey Jackson, one of the Governing Body members, was presiding over this meeting. | Geoffrey Jackson, a member of the Governing Body, was in charge of this meeting.

src_text: Nan pita, lè Elicha tounen bò Jouden an li frape dlo rivyè a ak rad Eliya a epi l rele byen fò, li di: "Kote Jewova, Bondye Eliya a?"
reference: Later, when Elisha returned to the Jordan, he struck the water of the river with Elijah's cloak and cried out, "Where is the Lord, the God of Elijah?"
explanation: It expresses a dramatic appeal for divine power and presence, showing Elisha invoking the same God who empowered Elijah to act again in a moment of need.
expected_translation: Later, when Elisha came back to the Jordan, he struck the river water with Elijah’s cloak and cried out, “Where is the Lord, the God of Elijah?” | When Elisha returned to the Jordan, he struck the water with Elijah’s cloak and called out, “Where is the Lord, the God of Elijah?”

src_text: Li fè lanèj tonbe kouvri latè tankou koton . Li fè lawouze tounen ti mòso glas sou tout pyebwa .
reference: He makes the snow fall like cotton and covers the earth like a blanket. He turns the dew into icicles on all the trees.
explanation: It poetically describes God’s power over nature, using vivid imagery of snow and frost to show how divine force can transform the world.
expected_translation: He makes snow fall like cotton and blanket the earth. | He turns dew into icicles on every tree.

src_text: Byenke alyans ak Abraram nan te reyalize yon fason literal pou desandan Abraram yo lè yo te antre nan Latè pwomiz, Ekriti yo montre alyans sa a t ap gen yon akonplisman espirityèl tou.
reference: Although the Abrahamic covenant was fulfilled in a literal way for Abraham's descendants when they entered the Promised Land, the Scriptures show that this covenant would also have a spiritual fulfillment.
explanation: The expression means that a promise once understood in a physical, historical sense is also seen as having a deeper spiritual meaning and fulfillment for believers.
expected_translation: Although the Abrahamic covenant was literally fulfilled for Abraham’s descendants when they entered the Promised Land, the Scriptures show that it would also have a spiritual fulfillment | While the Abrahamic covenant was fulfilled literally for Abraham’s descendants when they entered the Promised Land, the Scriptures indicate that it would also be fulfilled spiritually

src_text: Lè mwen panse ak 69 ane maryaj mwen gen ak Edith yo, mwen sonje Pwovèb 18: 22 ki di: "Lè yon nonm jwenn yon bon madanm, se yon bon bagay."
reference: When I think of my 69 years of marriage to Edith, I am reminded of Proverbs 18:22, which says: “A man finds a good wife—that is a good thing.”
explanation: The expression reflects a cultural value that sees a long, faithful marriage as a blessing and honors a good spouse as a source of stability, gratitude, and life’s success.
expected_translation: When I reflect on my 69 years of marriage to Edith, I’m reminded of Proverbs 18:22: “Finding a good wife is a blessing.” | Looking back on my 69 years with Edith, I think of Proverbs 18:22: “A good wife is a true blessing.”

src_text: Dezyèmman, sa nou rete ap gade kapab ranfòse dezi ki nan kè nou swa an byen, swa an mal.
reference: Second, what we watch can strengthen the desires of our hearts, for good or for evil.
explanation: It means that what people choose to focus on or consume can shape their inner desires and moral direction, either positively or negatively.
expected_translation: Second, what we watch can either strengthen our good desires or our bad ones. | Second, what we look at can feed the desires in our hearts, for better or worse.

src_text: Imajine w te la pandan Pòl t ap pale konsènan "Bondye ki fè monn nan ak tout sa ki ladan l" lan, epi annapre, li fè konnen Bondye sa a"pa abite nan tanp moun fè ak men".
reference: Imagine being there as Paul spoke about “the God who made the world and all the things in it,” and then he explained that this God “does not dwell in temples made with hands.”
explanation: It means that God is understood as greater than any human-built religious structure and cannot be confined to a physical temple.
expected_translation: Imagine being there when Paul spoke about “the God who made the world and everything in it,” and then said that this God “does not live in temples made by human hands” | Picture yourself there as Paul talked about “the God who made the world and everything in it,” and then explained that this God “does not dwell in temples built by human hands”

src_text: Kòm repons, Simon te di: "Mwen ta sipoze se sa li anile plis dèt pou li a."
reference: In response, Simon said: "I suppose that's the one he canceled the most debt for."
explanation: It means Simon is making a cautious, conversational guess about which person benefited most from debt forgiveness, reflecting a common way of speaking indirectly when inferring someone’s actions or motives.
expected_translation: I guess that’s the one he forgave the most debt for. | I suppose that’s the one he canceled the most debt for.

src_text: Men , fòk pasyans sa a fin fè travay li nèt pou nou kapab bon nèt sou tout pwen , byen devlope , san nou pa manke anyen .
reference: But let patience have her perfect work, that we may be perfect and complete, lacking nothing.
explanation: It conveys the idea that enduring hardship with patience helps a person mature fully and become spiritually and emotionally complete, without lacking anything important.
expected_translation: But let patience do its full work in us, so we may be fully mature and complete, lacking nothing. | Let patience finish its work so we can be whole, well-developed, and lacking nothing.

src_text: Yon fason klè, sa montre fèt Pak se pa yon fèt kretyen dwe selebre.
reference: Clearly, this shows that Easter is not a Christian holiday to be celebrated.
explanation: This expresses a religious viewpoint that Easter should not be observed by Christians because it is seen as lacking true Christian basis.
expected_translation: Clearly, this shows Easter is not a Christian holiday to celebrate. | Clearly, this shows that Easter should not be celebrated as a Christian holiday.

src_text: Gen ladan yo k'ap preche Kris la paske yo gen jalouzi nan kè yo . Gen lòt menm , se pou fè moun konkirans . Men gen lòt tou k'ap preche ak bon santiman .
reference: Some preach Christ out of envy , some out of rivalry , and some out of good will .
